title: Software Architecture & Engineering
rules: Prefer boring, proven technology over novel dependencies for critical paths.
Every module must be independently testable; no hidden global state.
Keep the typed boundary at the edges: validate inputs, trust internals.
Design for reversibility: migrations, feature flags and rollbacks before launches.
SOLID at class level, but prefer composition and pure functions over inheritance trees.
Never store secrets in code, logs or diffs; use environment variables.
Coverage is a proxy, not a goal: critical paths need explicit tests, not 100% totals.
checklist: Does every new module have at least one unit test on the happy path and one on failure?
Is there a single source of truth for each piece of state?
Are timeouts and cancellation propagated to every network call?
Is the error path user-visible and actionable?
Can this change be reverted with one commit or one flag?
Is the public API documented in the README or a spec file?
Does CI run typecheck, tests and build on every PR?

scoringRubric.1-3: Fragile: no tests, unclear boundaries, hidden coupling, no rollback path.
scoringRubric.4-6: Workable: partial coverage, some coupling, manual rollback, unclear ownership.
scoringRubric.7-8: Strong: typed boundaries, tested critical paths, feature-flagged, documented.
scoringRubric.9-10: Bulletproof: invariant checks, fuzz/edge tests, observability, automated rollback.
